NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Platform Engineer | Site Reliability Engineer
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior platform and site reliability engineer with over 10 years of infrastructure experience, including production Kubernetes on AWS. Tech lead experienced in cloud infrastructure operation, Terraform, developer platforms, observability and incident management. Delivered self-service infrastructure, improved service reliability and reduced cloud costs while working with product teams and leadership.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Kubernetes, Linux, Terraform, Atlantis, Puppet
Platform engineering: Argo CD, Crossplane, Karpenter, Helm, Kustomize, GitHub Actions, Backstage catalog
Observability and reliability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, Sloth, PagerDuty, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and testing: Go, Python, Bash, k6

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd | Apr 2022–Present
B2B accounting SaaS
- Tech lead for a five-person platform team operating eight EKS clusters across three regions and approximately 350 services.
- Built an internal developer platform with golden-path Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3. Reduced time from new service to production from around two weeks to under one day; adopted by all 14 product teams.
- Introduced SLOs and burn-rate alerts for 20 critical services and agreed an error-budget policy with product leadership. Reduced on-call pages by approximately 60% per week.
- Migrated node provisioning to Karpenter and AWS Spot for stateless workloads, including interruption handling. Reduced EC2 spend by 38%, approximately £410,000 per year.
- Served in the incident commander rotation and wrote the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games | Jan 2019–Mar 2022
- Operated AWS infrastructure using EC2, ECS and EKS for game backends serving up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure with Terraform, building approximately 40 modules and using Atlantis for pull-request plan and apply workflows.
- Replaced Nagios monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki.
- Led capacity planning for two major launches. Used k6 to simulate 300,000 concurrent players and identified and fixed a connection-pool limit before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting | Jul 2016–Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operations in Bash and Python and participated in on-call support for customer incidents.

ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
- Mentored three backend engineers transitioning into SRE.
- Built an open-source Kubernetes controller in Go to delete expired preview namespaces; approximately 120 GitHub stars.
- Presented “SLOs that product managers care about” at a UK DevOps meetup in 2024.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

LANGUAGES
English (native); Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear seniority, relevant achievements, credible metrics and substantial technical detail. The progression from Linux Systems Engineer to Site Reliability Engineer and then Senior Platform Engineer is easy to follow. The strongest evidence includes leading a five-person platform team, operating eight EKS clusters, adopting the internal developer platform across 14 product teams, reducing on-call pages by approximately 60%, and reducing EC2 spend by 38%. The document is professional and appropriately concise. The main content weakness is that systems architecture and design are implied through delivery examples but not stated explicitly, which slightly reduces alignment with a role focused on shaping architecture from the start.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional headings, chronological experience, readable text formatting, standard technology names and measurable achievement statements. It should parse reliably because it avoids tables, columns, graphics and unusual section labels. AI screening probability is high for the AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, platform engineering, observability, reliability and technical leadership aspects of the role. Screening strength is reduced because Terragrunt and mTLS/SSL/TLS are not present; these are genuine gaps in the candidate information and must not be added without evidence. Adding explicit, truthful wording around cloud infrastructure design and systems architecture would improve semantic matching. The skills section is already detailed, although some tools such as Sloth and PagerDuty appear in the CV through the experience content rather than the technical skills section.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud operation, Terraform, Linux, virtual machines through EC2, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, analytical problem-solving, observability, reliability and clear communication. It also reflects Corvale's engineering-led culture through ownership of platforms end to end, self-service enablement, collaboration with product leadership and practical operational improvements. The candidate's experience with Go and Python service templates provides relevant backend exposure. The candidate information does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mutual TLS, SSL/TLS, IoT, automotive or remote-device integration, or JVM experience. These are capability gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The CV also does not provide direct evidence of train-to-cloud communication, certificate management or agreements with external manufacturers' engineers.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENT:
1. In the Professional Summary, change "Tech lead experienced in cloud infrastructure operation, Terraform, developer platforms, observability and incident management" to "Tech lead experienced in cloud infrastructure design and operation, systems architecture, Terraform, developer platforms, observability and incident management." This is supported by designing and building the internal developer platform, operating EKS infrastructure and holding the AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional certification.
2. In the Senior Platform Engineer experience entry at Tallybrook Ltd, change "Built an internal developer platform" to "Designed and built an internal developer platform". This makes the systems-design contribution explicit without claiming unsupported architecture responsibilities.
3. In the Technical Skills section, consider changing the category label "Cloud and infrastructure" to "Cloud infrastructure and systems architecture". Retain the existing technologies and do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, IoT or certificate management, as these are not supported by the candidate information.
4. For strict factual consistency with the Original Candidate Information, change "over 10 years of infrastructure experience" in the Professional Summary to "10 years of infrastructure experience" unless the candidate has independently verified a longer total period.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from Linux systems engineering to senior platform leadership. The summary is concise and credible, while the experience section uses specific scale and outcomes: eight EKS clusters, approximately 350 services, 14 product teams, 60% fewer pages, and £410,000 annual EC2 savings. The document demonstrates ownership, technical leadership, reliability thinking, and effective communication without overstating formal people-management responsibilities. The main content limitation is that some relevant capabilities are represented only through keyword lists rather than explicit context, particularly system design, stakeholder engagement, and networking/security practices.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is very good. The document uses standard section headings, chronological experience, readable text formatting, consistent dates, and no tables, graphics, headers/footers, or unusual layout elements that would interfere with parsing. It contains strong keywords for AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, Terraform, infrastructure as code, GitOps, observability, SLOs, incident management, Linux, and technical leadership. AI screening probability is high for general AWS/platform/SRE roles and reasonably high for this role, but may be reduced for exact-match screening because Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, and IoT or remote-device integration are not present. Those are candidate-experience gaps rather than document defects and should not be added without supporting evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with the core infrastructure, AWS, systems architecture, reliability, technical leadership, analytical thinking, and communication requirements. It shows hands-on cloud environment design and operation through EKS, EC2, Terraform, Crossplane, Karpenter, and AWS services; strong Terraform through approximately 40 modules and Atlantis workflows; and stakeholder engagement through error-budget policy agreed with product leadership and adoption by all 14 product teams. AWS, Linux, and virtual-machine-related infrastructure are well represented. The candidate's material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, or JVM experience, so these are gaps against the role rather than CV-writing problems. The document does not specifically demonstrate train-to-cloud connectivity, collaboration with equipment manufacturers, or fleet/remote-device systems, but its platform, observability, incident-management, and backend-service enablement experience is transferable. The leadership and ownership evidence fits Corvale's engineering-led, collaborative culture without making unsupported claims about the company's values.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ATS/alignment enhancement: In the Professional Summary section, revise the sentence beginning "Tech lead experienced in cloud infrastructure design and operation" to explicitly include the ad's supported terminology "system design" and "stakeholder engagement." For example: "Technical lead experienced in hands-on cloud infrastructure design and operation, systems architecture and system design, Terraform-based infrastructure as code, developer platforms, observability, incident management, and stakeholder engagement with product teams and leadership." This accurately reflects the existing evidence and improves exact-term matching without adding unsupported skills.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise and highly credible CV. It has a clear senior positioning, a relevant professional summary, logical section headings, strong quantified achievements and excellent evidence of platform ownership. The experience bullets demonstrate meaningful outcomes: faster service delivery, lower on-call volume, substantial cloud-cost reduction and operation at significant scale. The document is also consistent with the Original Candidate Information; no unsupported skills, certifications or experiences were identified. The main limitations are role-specific coverage gaps rather than writing or structure defects: there is no evidence of Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, IoT or remote-device integration, or a specific security initiative.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional headings, readable text, standard reverse-chronological experience, searchable technology names and measurable achievements. AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, EKS, Linux, system design, incident management, observability and stakeholder engagement are visible in relevant sections. AI screening probability is high for the platform engineering, AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, reliability and technical-leadership aspects of the role, but lower for exact searches involving Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT, remote devices and fleet connectivity. These absent terms should not be added because they are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a strong match for hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud environment operation, Terraform, systems design, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, reliability and clear analytical communication. The internal developer platform, SLO programme, incident leadership and capacity-planning examples also align well with Corvale's engineering-led, ownership-oriented and collaborative environment. The candidate's material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, practical security work beyond listed AWS IAM and networking components, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, or fleet connectivity. These are genuine capability or evidence gaps, not defects that can be solved by CV wording. Backend exposure is present through Go and Python service templates, although there is no JVM experience shown. Linux and virtual-machine/infrastructure experience are well supported through Linux server administration and EC2 operations.
critique.improvement_instructions: Minor enhancement only: In the Professional Summary section, change "Tech lead experienced in cloud infrastructure design and operation, system design, Terraform, developer platforms, observability, incident management and stakeholder engagement" to "Technical lead experienced in cloud infrastructure design and operation, systems architecture and system design, Terraform, developer platforms, observability, incident management and stakeholder engagement." This uses the job advertisement's exact "systems architecture" and "technical leadership" terminology while remaining supported by the internal developer platform architecture, EKS operation and technical-lead experience already documented. In the Senior Platform Engineer experience entry, change "Designed and built an internal developer platform" to "Designed the architecture and built an internal developer platform" to make the existing systems-design evidence more explicit without adding a new claim.
